summary: B. N. Goswamy was an Indian scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Panjab University (~1952–1958), later serving in the Indian Administrative Service (~1956–1958) and on the faculty of Panjab University (~1965–1993).

B. N. K. Sharma specialized in Indology and philosophy. He earned degrees from the University of Madras and Presidency College, Chennai, and studied under Satyadhyana Tirtha. His career included posts at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, and Ramnarain Ruia College.

B. R. Ambedkar worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia University, the London School of Economics, and Gray's Inn under scholars including John Dewey and Edwin Cannan, later serving as principal of Government Law College, Mumbai.

B. R. Gopal was an Indologist and historian. He served as Technical Research Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1964), Epigraphical Assistant to the Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1965), and Epigraphist for Epigraphia Carnatica (attested 1974).

Baatr Kitinov works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. in World History at Moscow State University and has served as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Baburam Saksena was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. An advanced student at Banaras Hindu University in 1921, he later served as Vice-Chancellor of Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University (~1964–1968).

Bahadur Chand Chhabra specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University, he held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966), Government Epigraphist for India (~1945–1953), and Panjab University (~1965–1973).
Baiei Henmi was a Japanese scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He was educated at Tokyo Imperial University and later served on the faculty at Tama Art University.

Baihui Wu worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1945–1951), Peking University (~1952–1957), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of Philosophy (~1978).

Baij Nath Puri was an Indian scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning his M.Litt. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford, he served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1956–1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Deccan College, Elphinstone College, and Government Law College, Mumbai, and later taught at the New English School (~1880–1885) and Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

Bal Krishen Thapar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of the Punjab, Heidelberg University, and under Mortimer Wheeler. He later served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981).
Bala Sahai Shastri was a scholar of Indology who held posts at Panjab University, including Assistant to the Librarian (attested 1932) and in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1947).

Baliram Shukla works in philosophy and Indology. He has held appointments at Savitribai Phule Pune University, including Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and Professor (attested 2026).
Balram Shukla is an Indian scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Delhi, where he became a professor around 2013.

Balthasar Bickel specializes in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Zurich (~1986–1997) and held positions at the University of Leipzig (~2002–2011) and the University of Zurich (~2011).

Bangwei Wang is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Peking University in 1987 and served there as Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies (attested 2000–2026).

Banikanta Kakati worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He later served as a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and as Dean of Arts at Gauhati University (1948).

Bapu Deva Sastri worked in Indology. He studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson, Dhundiraja Misra, and Sevarama, and later taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara A. Holdrege specializes in religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, including Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and Professor (attested 2026).
